objective: Prove: (1) on every two-kind sphere with local Kasteleyn signs the frames are flat except at the six digons, each of label holonomy -1, so a flat state with exactly one violated line exists wherever six disjoint cut paths reach the corners; (2) the reduction of one-sided Sperner_m of FLAT-STATES-20261107-001B applies to any corner-free lattice triangle of side 2m with such cut paths, so with SPHERE-WIDTH-20261107-001B the knot needs resolution width at least c*m; (3) hence width at least c'*r, where r is the radius of the largest flat disc, and at most O(sqrt n): fat spheres need width Theta(sqrt n) whether or not they are round. Check the holonomies and flat states on octahedral spheres, tubes and grown spheres; measure flat radii, elimination widths and the cut paths.
status: Proved 2026-11-07: on every two-kind sphere the frames are flat at three-point faces with label holonomy -1 at the six digons, so flat states exist wherever cut paths reach the digons; the Sperner reduction then needs only a corner-free lattice triangle and its cut paths, giving resolution width at least c times the flat radius (and at most O(sqrt n)); grown lopsided spheres have flat radius 0.14 to 0.35 sqrt(n) in the sample, against 0.25 sqrt(n) on the octahedral spheres.
title: The Sperner reduction needs only a flat disc
